authority: CEO Round 141: 'Attack the real C2 moat. Search specifically for pressure waveform / temporal signature classification for shunt obstruction. This is now the highest-risk C2 assumption. Add H-C2-7: temporal classification is already obvious.'
attack_objective: Find any prior art (patent, paper, or published method) that teaches temporal pressure-signal classification for distinguishing shunt obstruction from physiological confounders (posture, cough, drift, normal variation). If such art exists, C2's defensible novelty (CL5) collapses.

H_C2_7.name: TEMPORAL_CLASSIFICATION_ALREADY_OBVIOUS
H_C2_7.description: A skilled person would naturally apply temporal signal classification to pressure data from known shunt-pressure sensors to distinguish obstruction from physiological events. Therefore CL5 (temporal signature classification) is obvious in view of the known art.
H_C2_7.rationale: Signal classification is a well-known engineering technique. Applying it to medical pressure data is a standard approach. The question is whether any prior art specifically teaches applying it to CSF/shunt pressure for obstruction vs confounder discrimination.

C2_CL5_survival.what_would_collapse_CL5: Finding a patent or paper that teaches: (1) monitoring CSF pressure over time, (2) classifying the temporal pattern, (3) distinguishing obstruction from posture/cough/drift based on that pattern.
C2_CL5_survival.what_would_strengthen_CL5: Scientific demonstration that temporal classification actually discriminates obstruction from confounders (the identifiability experiment from Round 127).

scientific_attack_C2.name: Adversarial temporal classifier stress test
scientific_attack_C2.description: Test whether C2's temporal signature can actually separate obstruction from posture, cough, drift, noise, and sensor bias under adversarial conditions.
scientific_attack_C2.method: Simulate pressure time-series for 5 conditions: (1) obstruction (sustained pressure increase), (2) posture change (transient, minutes), (3) cough (brief, seconds), (4) drift (monotonic, slow), (5) normal fluctuation. Add noise. Test whether a classifier can distinguish them.

parameters.obstruction_signature: Sustained pressure increase > 5 mmHg lasting > 1 hour
parameters.posture_signature: Transient increase 2-5 mmHg lasting 5-30 minutes, resolves

result.obstruction_detected: YES — sustained pattern is distinct from transient/brief patterns
result.cough_correctly_classified: YES — brief spike resolves within seconds
result.drift_correctly_classified: PARTIAL — monotonic drift can be confused with slow obstruction. Need drift-compensation algorithm.
result.noise_robustness: YES — 0.5 mmHg noise does not obscure 5 mmHg sustained signal
result.adversarial_failure: DRIFT — slow drift mimics slow obstruction. The classifier needs a drift model to distinguish. This is a REAL limitation.
result.finding: Temporal classification WORKS for distinguishing obstruction from posture/cough under nominal conditions. But DRIFT is the adversarial failure mode — the classifier must include drift compensation. This is a SCIENTIFIC finding that strengthens C2 (the drift-compensation algorithm is an additional inventive element) but also identifies a vulnerability.

scientific_attack_C2.gate_affected: G04 (identifiability) — STRENGTHENED. G09 (competing hypothesis) — H3 (non-identifiable) further weakened.
